g12-ch10-board-01.q: Find the unit vector in the direction of the sum of $\vec a=2\hat i+2\hat j-5\hat k$ and $\vec b=2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$.
g12-ch10-board-01.s: $\vec a+\vec b=4\hat i+3\hat j-2\hat k$ [1]. Its magnitude is $\sqrt{29}$, so the unit vector is $\frac1{\sqrt{29}}(4\hat i+3\hat j-2\hat k)$ [1].

alt.q: Find the vector of magnitude $8$ in the direction of $5\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$.
alt.s: The magnitude is $\sqrt{30}$ [1]. Multiply the unit vector by $8$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-01.q: Find the angle between $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$.
Show that $2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$, $\hat i-3\hat j-5\hat k$ and $3\hat i-4\hat j-4\hat k$ form the sides of a right triangle.
g12-ch10-board-01.s: The first two add to the third, so the vectors form a triangle [1]. $(2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k)\cdot(\hat i-3\hat j-5\hat k)=2+3-5=0$, so the angle between them is a right angle [1].

g12-ch10-board-01.q: $\vec a=5\hat i-\hat j-3\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i+3\hat j-5\hat k$. Show that $\vec a+\vec b$ and $\vec a-\vec b$ are perpendicular.
g12-ch10-board-01.s: $\vec a+\vec b=6\hat i+2\hat j-8\hat k$ [1]. $\vec a-\vec b=4\hat i-4\hat j+2\hat k$ [1]. The scalar product is $24-8-16=0$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-01.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A(1,1,2)$, $B(2,3,5)$ and $C(1,5,5)$.
g12-ch10-board-01.s: $\overrightarrow{AB}=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=4\hat j+3\hat k$ [1]. $\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}=-6\hat i-3\hat j+4\hat k$ [1]. Area $=\frac12\sqrt{36+9+16}=\frac{\sqrt{61}}2$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-01.q: $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$. Find a unit vector perpendicular to both $\vec a+\vec b$ and $\vec a-\vec b$.
g12-ch10-board-01.s: $\vec a+\vec b=2\hat i+3\hat j+4\hat k$ and $\vec a-\vec b=-\hat j-2\hat k$ [1]. Their cross product is $-2\hat i+4\hat j-2\hat k$ [1]. Divide by $2\sqrt6$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-01.q: $\vec a=\hat i+4\hat j+2\hat k$, $\vec b=3\hat i-2\hat j+7\hat k$ and $\vec c=2\hat i-\hat j+4\hat k$. Find a vector $\vec d$ perpendicular to both $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ with $\vec c\cdot\vec d=15$.
g12-ch10-board-01.s: $\vec d=\lambda(\vec a\times\vec b)$ [1]. $\vec a\times\vec b=32\hat i-\hat j-14\hat k$ [2]. $\vec c\cdot(\vec a\times\vec b)=64+1-56=9$, so $9\lambda=15$ [1]. $\lambda=\frac53$ [1].

alt.q: Show that the points $A(-2\hat i+3\hat j+5\hat k)$, $B(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)$ and $C(7\hat i-\hat k)$ are collinear.
alt.s: $\overrightarrow{AB}=3\hat i-\hat j-2\hat k$ [2]. $\overrightarrow{BC}=6\hat i-2\hat j-4\hat k$ [2]. $\overrightarrow{BC}=2\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $B$ is common, so the points are collinear [1].

g12-ch10-board-01.q: Case study. A drone flies in a straight line from $A(1,2,3)$ to $B(4,6,3)$ (in km). (i) Write $\overrightarrow{AB}$. [1] (ii) Find the distance $AB$. [1] (iii) Find the direction cosines of $\overrightarrow{AB}$. [2] \textbf{OR} (iii) A wind force $\vec F=2\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ acts along the flight. Find the work done by $\vec F$. [2]
g12-ch10-board-01.s: (i) $\vec b-\vec a=3\hat i+4\hat j$ [1]. (ii) $\sqrt{9+16}=5$ [1]. (iii) Divide by $5$ [1]: $\frac35,\frac45,0$ [1]. OR $\vec F\cdot\overrightarrow{AB}$ [1] $=6+4+0=10$ [1].

alt.s: The first is twice the second [1]: $6=-2\lambda$, so $\lambda=-3$ [1].

Show that $|\vec a|\vec b+|\vec b|\vec a$ is perpendicular to $|\vec a|\vec b-|\vec b|\vec a$, for non-zero $\vec a$ and $\vec b$.
g12-ch10-board-02.s: The scalar product is $|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2-|\vec b|^2|\vec a|^2$ [2], because the middle terms cancel. It is $0$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-02.q: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A(1,2,3)$, $B(2,-1,4)$ and $C(4,5,-1)$.
g12-ch10-board-02.s: $\overrightarrow{AB}=\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=3\hat i+3\hat j-4\hat k$ [1]. Their cross product is $9\hat i+7\hat j+12\hat k$ [1]. Area $=\frac12\sqrt{81+49+144}$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-02.q: $\vec a$, $\vec b$, $\vec c$ are unit vectors with $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$. Find $\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a$.
g12-ch10-board-02.s: $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=0$ [1]. $3+2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a)=0$ [1]. The sum is $-\frac32$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-02.q: $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$ and $\vec b=\hat j-\hat k$. Find $\vec c$ such that $\vec a\times\vec c=\vec b$ and $\vec a\cdot\vec c=3$.
g12-ch10-board-02.s: Let $\vec c=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k$ [1]. $\vec a\times\vec c=(z-y)\hat i+(x-z)\hat j+(y-x)\hat k=\hat j-\hat k$ gives $z=y$ and $x=y+1$ [2]. $x+y+z=3$ gives $y=\frac23$ [1]. $\vec c=\frac53\hat i+\frac23\hat j+\frac23\hat k$ [1].

alt.q: Find a vector of magnitude $6$ perpendicular to both $2\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$ and $\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$.
alt.s: The cross product is $\hat i-5\hat j-3\hat k$ [2]. Its magnitude is $\sqrt{35}$ [1]. The required vectors are $\pm\frac6{\sqrt{35}}(\hat i-5\hat j-3\hat k)$ [2].

g12-ch10-board-02.q: Case study. Three tents stand at $P(1,-2,3)$, $Q(3,1,2)$ and $R(2,0,4)$. (i) Write $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{PR}$. [1] (ii) Find $|\overrightarrow{PQ}|$. [1] (iii) Find the area of the triangle $PQR$. [2] \textbf{OR} (iii) Find the cosine of the angle $QPR$. [2]
g12-ch10-board-02.a: (i) $2\hat i+3\hat j-\hat k$, $\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k$; (ii) $\sqrt{14}$; (iii) $\frac{\sqrt{35}}2$; OR $\frac{\sqrt{21}}6$.
g12-ch10-board-02.s: (i) $\overrightarrow{PQ}=2\hat i+3\hat j-\hat k$, $\overrightarrow{PR}=\hat i+2\hat j+\hat k$ [1]. (ii) $\sqrt{4+9+1}$ [1]. (iii) The cross product is $5\hat i-3\hat j+\hat k$ [1]; area $\frac{\sqrt{35}}2$ [1]. OR The scalar product is $2+6-1=7$ [1]; $\cos\theta=\frac7{\sqrt{14}\sqrt6}=\frac{\sqrt{21}}6$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-03.s: $\vec a+\vec b=3\hat i+\hat j$ with magnitude $\sqrt{10}$ [1]. The vector is $\frac5{\sqrt{10}}(3\hat i+\hat j)$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-03.q: $|\vec a|=3$, $|\vec b|=\frac23$ and $\vec a\times\vec b$ is a unit vector. Find the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$.
g12-ch10-board-03.s: $|\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta=1$ [1]. $2\sin\theta=1$, so $\theta=\frac\pi6$ [1].

Using vectors, show that $A(2,-1,3)$, $B(4,3,1)$ and $C(3,1,2)$ are collinear.
g12-ch10-board-03.s: $\overrightarrow{AB}=2\hat i+4\hat j-2\hat k$ [1]. $\overrightarrow{AC}=\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$ [1]. $\overrightarrow{AB}=2\overrightarrow{AC}$ with $A$ common [1].

g12-ch10-board-03.q: Find the area of the parallelogram whose diagonals are $2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$ and $3\hat i+4\hat j-\hat k$.
g12-ch10-board-03.s: Area $=\frac12|\vec d_1\times\vec d_2|$ [1]. $\vec d_1\times\vec d_2=-3\hat i+5\hat j+11\hat k$ [1]. Area $=\frac12\sqrt{9+25+121}$ [1].

g12-ch10-board-03.q: $\vec a\times\vec b=\vec c\times\vec d$ and $\vec a\times\vec c=\vec b\times\vec d$. Show that $\vec a-\vec d$ is parallel to $\vec b-\vec c$, when they are non-zero.
g12-ch10-board-03.s: $(\vec a-\vec d)\times(\vec b-\vec c)=\vec a\times\vec b-\vec a\times\vec c-\vec d\times\vec b+\vec d\times\vec c$ [1]. Substitute: $\vec c\times\vec d-\vec b\times\vec d+\vec b\times\vec d-\vec c\times\vec d=\vec 0$ [1]. A zero cross product means parallel [1].

g12-ch10-board-03.q: Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane of the triangle $A(3,-1,2)$, $B(1,-1,-3)$, $C(4,-3,1)$, and find the area of the triangle.
g12-ch10-board-03.s: $\overrightarrow{AB}=-2\hat i-5\hat k$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}=\hat i-2\hat j-\hat k$ [1]. Cross product $-10\hat i-7\hat j+4\hat k$ [2]. Magnitude $\sqrt{165}$, so the unit vectors are $\pm\frac1{\sqrt{165}}(-10\hat i-7\hat j+4\hat k)$ [1]. Area $\frac{\sqrt{165}}2$ [1].

alt.q: $|\vec a|=3$, $|\vec b|=4$, $|\vec c|=5$, and each vector is perpendicular to the sum of the other two. Find $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|$.
alt.s: $\vec a\cdot(\vec b+\vec c)=0$, $\vec b\cdot(\vec c+\vec a)=0$, $\vec c\cdot(\vec a+\vec b)=0$ [2]. Adding: $2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a)=0$ [1]. $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=9+16+25=50$ [2].

g12-ch10-board-03.q: Case study. A force $\vec F=2\hat i+\hat j+3\hat k$ moves a box from $P(1,0,2)$ to $Q(4,2,1)$. (i) Write the displacement $\vec d=\overrightarrow{PQ}$. [1] (ii) Find the work done. [1] (iii) Find the projection of $\vec F$ on $\vec d$. [2] \textbf{OR} (iii) Find a unit vector perpendicular to both $\vec F$ and $\vec d$. [2]
g12-ch10-board-03.a: (i) $3\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$; (ii) $5$; (iii) $\frac5{\sqrt{14}}$; OR $\pm\frac1{3\sqrt{19}}(-7\hat i+11\hat j+\hat k)$.
g12-ch10-board-03.s: (i) $3\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k$ [1]. (ii) $6+2-3=5$ [1]. (iii) $\frac{\vec F\cdot\vec d}{|\vec d|}$ [1] $=\frac5{\sqrt{14}}$ [1]. OR $\vec F\times\vec d=-7\hat i+11\hat j+\hat k$ [1]; divide by $\sqrt{171}=3\sqrt{19}$ [1].
